paper.title_en: Structure and decay of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-condensate candidates from cluster effective field theory interactions
paper.abstract_en: Dilute gas-like configurations of <math><mi>α</mi></math> particles, often termed <math><mi>α</mi></math> condensates, have been proposed to exist in certain excited states of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-conjugate nuclei. This work investigates the structural and decay properties of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-condensate candidates within a few-body framework using leading-order cluster effective field theory interactions. To isolate dilute <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> configurations, a constrained model space strategy is implemented inspired by Yamada and Schuck [Phys. Rev. C 69, 024309 (2004)], which constructs a description specifically for suprathreshold states. By explicitly decoupling the nonuniversal, compact configurations lying below the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> threshold, this framework describes <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> condensates as quasibound states localized within the Coulomb barrier. The stochastic variational method is used to perform theoretical calculations for the proposed <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> condensates ranging from <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> to <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ne</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>20</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The results not only map the formation of these novel cluster states in heavier <math><mi>α</mi></math>-conjugate nuclei but also offer critical insights into the applicability of few-body universality to charged particles.
